STP.note: Civil registry is used only for client identification by Ke-Non, not a civil register to ID link.
Civil registry named only as a client-identification source; no digital registration stated.
School-attendance verification with the Ministry of Education is a social protection link, and its monitoring module is listed for phase 3.
A complaints mechanism is only planned for phase 2 of Ke-Non, with no launch stated.

facts.fact: openIMIS says the government's Ke-Non system, adopted in May 2023, includes a payments module working with Banco Internacional de Sao Tome e Principe for the conditional cash transfer programme.
openIMIS says Ke-Non, which holds the Unique Social Registry and the payments module, identifies clients against the national civil registry of the Ministry of Justice.

STP.note: Nothing on a number at birth.
Nothing on refugees or displaced people.
Nothing on local civil registration offices.
Nothing on mobile money or retail payments.
Nothing on tax or fee payment.

facts.fact: openIMIS says Ke-Non has links to partners' data systems: Banco Internacional de Sao Tome e Principe for payments and the Ministry of Justice national civil registry for client identification.

openIMIS says the government adopted Ke-Non, built on CORE-MIS and openIMIS, in May 2023 to manage the national social protection system and its conditional cash transfer programme, housed at the Institute of Innovation and Knowledge.
openIMIS says Ke-Non's payment module works with Banco Internacional de Sao Tome e Principe for the conditional cash transfer programme.
openIMIS says Ke-Non holds a Unique Social Registry database, whose data for more than 10,000 families eligible for the cash transfer were updated between December 2023 and February 2024.
